pixel: one art pixel per screen pixel (as ui_icons, sheet 1): draw at 1x on a 1600x900 screen, @2x on a 2x screen, always with image-rendering: pixelated

frame.from: ui_icons (sheet 1), read only: skill_slot_steel.png and skill_slot_steel_active.png, 56x56, the icon window 44x44 at 6,6; see ui_icons/manifest.json for its slices

method: his sheets are pixel art (480x268 scaled 4.1667x and saved as JPEG); his pixels are taken back first (tools/refs/icons-from-ref-23.py). 88: his own pixels one to one (his 90x90 or 93x91 window with the columns and rows that show least dropped), on a palette sampled from his pixels, 1-2 pixel areas merged only where his own pixels do not stand out. 44: area mean of his pixels, except his thin lines and strongest specks, which keep their own colour one pixel wide; a light bilateral filter, nearest palette entry, 1-2 pixel areas merged; then hand-fixes only where that still loses his picture (see tools/ui/ui-icons-23.ts). Sheets 8 to 11 use no bilateral filter (it lightened his dark figures into his ground), and their palettes give his rare colours a slot each: after the k-means, every colour of the 44's and the 88's pictures still far from the palette in hue (his skin, his violet chains, a dragon's teeth, his greys and whites) is grouped and the group missed most gets its own entry, his nearest real colour, up to 20 (paletteCovered); his thin marks of one colour (skin, violet chains, embers, teeth, mouth cores, foam) are kept by colour rules. Sheets 8 and 11 have bigger windows (127 to 139 of his pixels across, not square): the icon is the square part of his window (cropInWindow; Swap keeps 139x127 and is squeezed 9% across so his two ninjas stay whole), and its 88 is made as its 44 (area mean of his pixels with his thin lines and specks kept, palette, clean-up: method88). Edits the owner asked for are listed per icon under edits: made on his window first, then drawn again crisp at 88 and 44
checks: small = 8-connected areas of one colour of 1 or 2 pixels: smallHis are his own marks (at 88 his pixel stands out there; at 44 his kept specks), smallDrawn hold a hand-fixed detail, smallOther are left over from the reduction; lowFreq = mean OKLab difference x100 to his box reduction after both are blurred (sigma size/30), lowFreqBoxOnPalette = the same for his box reduction put on our palette; ssim = structural similarity of the lightness (Gaussian window sigma 1.5) to his picture box-reduced to 88, ours (the 44 shown 2x) against ssimBox, his own box reduction to 44 shown 2x; hue = OKLab median hue in degrees (hueHis: his box reduction); thinRun = the longest straight run of one colour one pixel thick [length, row or col, index]
